title: Top 5 Terror
subtitle: Who are the TOP players — and are they for real?
conceptSummary: LIMIT N shows only the first N rows — perfect for top-10 lists.

dialogue.text: We need the Top 5 highest-scoring stats — just the top 5, not all 15.
LIMIT. Use LIMIT. It's literally called LIMIT because it limits the results.
The Chief has a way with words. Use LIMIT 5 at the end of your query!

teachMoment.title: LIMIT: Cut the List
teachMoment.body:
LIMIT cuts your results to a set number:

SELECT * FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC LIMIT 5

This gets the TOP 5 scores. Always use ORDER BY with LIMIT so you get the right top/bottom items.

task.instruction: Get the TOP 5 match stats by runs_scored (highest first). Show stat_id, player_id, and runs_scored.
task.startingQuery: SELECT stat_id, player_id, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC LIMIT 5
task.solution: SELECT stat_id, player_id, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC LIMIT 5

hints.text: First sort by runs_scored DESC, then add LIMIT at the very end.
The pattern is: SELECT ... FROM ... ORDER BY runs_scored DESC LIMIT 5
Full: SELECT stat_id, player_id, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC LIMIT 5

winDialogue.text: Top 5 scores confirmed. And player_id 1 appears THREE times in the top 5... all suspicious matches.
That's Arjun Patel from Mumbai Warriors. We need to dig deeper into his record. Next world: SQL Streets.

storyBeat: Player 1, Arjun Patel, has suspiciously high stats in specific matches. Someone is inflating his numbers. To track them, we need more SQL power. Time to level up.
